sections.title: FinSight
sections.subtitle: Conversational analysis and reporting over financial data.

sections.heading: Ask questions of financial data
sections.body:
Finance and reporting teams need to explain what a number means as well as produce it. FinSight supports conversational analysis and reporting over financial data across business reporting needs.

Start with a defined reporting question and an agreed dataset. Review the evidence behind the answer before using it to inform a business decision.

[Request a FinSight demo](#get-in-touch) · [View all products](/products-and-accelerators)
sections.secondaryHeading: Financial analysis with a defined data scope
sections.secondaryBody:
FinSight is part of [Data & AI](/services/data-ai). [Data platforms & analytics](/services/data-ai/data-platforms-analytics) supports the surrounding pipelines and reporting estate; [AI strategy & governance](/services/data-ai/ai-strategy-governance) helps establish ownership and controls.

The product is analytical assistance. It is not a statement of regulated financial advice or regulatory-reporting compliance.

sections.heading: Conversational analysis and reporting
sections.description: Two distinct tasks: explore a financial question and turn the analysis into reporting. Agree sources, definitions and review criteria during evaluation.

items.title: Ask a financial question
items.description: Use a question to explore an agreed financial dataset. For example, evaluate a question about movement between reporting periods, with the period, entity and measure defined first.
items.bullets:
Input – reporting question and approved dataset
Evaluation output – an answer checked against expected calculations

items.title: Review and report
items.description: Use the analysis in a reporting workflow, with a finance reviewer checking the figures and narrative. Confirm which report outputs and any chart or export formats the product supports.
items.bullets:
Input – reviewed analysis and reporting requirements
Evaluation output – a sample report with reconciliation checks

sections.heading: From financial data to a reviewed report
sections.description: Evaluation workflow, using approved sample financial data: establish the source, ask a question, reconcile the result and assess the reporting output.

items.title: Define the dataset
items.description: Identify source data, reporting periods, entities and measures. Establish freshness and data-grain requirements before connection or import.

items.title: Ask the question
items.description: Use a representative reporting question with agreed business definitions. Demonstrate the supported question-to-answer workflow.

items.title: Reconcile the figures
items.description: Compare the answer with reviewer-calculated reference values. Investigate differences and record calculation ownership.

items.title: Review the report
items.description: Assess the produced reporting output and supported formats. Retain human approval for financial interpretation and distribution.

sections.heading: Example: a management-reporting question
sections.body:
**Illustrative example, not a client case study.** A finance team asks: “How did operating expenses change between the two reporting periods?” Define the periods, expense measure and entity scope in an agreed management dataset before evaluating the conversational analysis.

The evaluation produces a metric dictionary, sample question and answer, a reviewed report and reconciliation checks. The finance owner remains accountable for data definitions, calculation review and the final interpretation.

Where reporting feeds wider operational redesign, explore [Intelligent Operations](/solutions/intelligent-operations).

sections.heading: Agree the financial-data and control scope
sections.description: Available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without Linkfields services. Bring a reporting question to a guided demo; use approved sample data, not sensitive financial records.

items.title: Which financial sources and outputs fit?
items.description: Review supported data sources, connectors and import methods against your estate. Agree data grain, freshness, reporting periods, currency and metric definitions. Confirm available report, chart and export formats before agreeing the scope of any downstream reporting integration.

items.title: Who owns calculation and reconciliation?
items.description: Finance owners define measures and reference calculations, and approve the interpretation. Confirm the source evidence and auditability available in the product. Agree reconciliation, exception handling and review responsibilities; analytical assistance does not establish regulatory compliance or provide regulated financial advice.

items.title: How is financial data protected?
items.description: Review access controls, tenant isolation, audit records, model-provider data use and data retention. Confirm hosting, residency and any restrictions on sensitive records before enterprise evaluation. An initial demo should not require confidential financial data.

items.title: How do licensing and support work?
items.description: Confirm available deployment options, licence or subscription terms and SaaS hosting scope for FinSight. Optional data integration, implementation and managed support are scoped separately. Agree onboarding, the product version included, responsibility for updates and support terms in the proposal.
